title: A Mittag-Leffler tower of nonempty sets has a nonempty limit (Stacks 0597, index set the positive integers)
statement: Let $(E_i,f_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an inverse system of sets [def-weil-inverse-system] (sets $E_i$ and maps $f_i:E_{i+1}\to E_i$), with composites $\varphi_{k,i}=f_i\circ f_{i+1}\circ\cdots\circ f_{k-1}:E_k\to E_i$ for $k\ge i$ ($\varphi_{i,i}=\mathrm{id}$). Assume that every $E_i$ is nonempty and that $(E_i)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition: for every $i\ge1$ there is an integer $c(i)\ge i$ such that $\varphi_{k,i}(E_k)=\varphi_{c(i),i}(E_{c(i)})$ (as subsets of $E_i$) for all $k\ge c(i)$. Then the limit $\varprojlim_iE_i=\{(x_i)_{i\ge1}\in\prod_{i\ge1}E_i: f_i(x_{i+1})=x_i\text{ for all }i\ge1\}$ is nonempty.

proof.text: For each $i\ge1$ put $B_i=\varphi_{c(i),i}(E_{c(i)})\subseteq E_i$. Every $B_i$ is nonempty because $E_{c(i)}$ is nonempty. The images $\varphi_{k,i}(E_k)$ decrease as $k$ increases, since $\varphi_{k,i}=\varphi_{j,i}\circ\varphi_{k,j}$ for $k\ge j\ge i$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. By the Mittag-Leffler hypothesis they equal $B_i$ for all $k\ge c(i)$, so $B_i=\bigcap_{k\ge i}\varphi_{k,i}(E_k)$; the terms with $i\le k<c(i)$ contain $B_i$ by the same composite identity.

source.place: Algebra, Definition 0595 (definition-ML-system) and Example 0596 (example-ML-surjective-maps), algebra.tex lines 20710--20745: stable images

proof.text: The restricted transition $f_i:B_{i+1}\to B_i$ is well defined: if $x\in B_{i+1}$, then $x=\varphi_{k,i+1}(z)$ for some $k\ge\max(c(i),c(i+1),i+1)$ and $z\in E_k$, by stabilization of the image at level $i+1$; hence $f_i(x)=\varphi_{k,i}(z)\in B_i$. It is surjective: for $y\in B_i$ choose the same kind of $k$; stabilization at $i$ gives $z\in E_k$ with $\varphi_{k,i}(z)=y$. Put $x=\varphi_{k,i+1}(z)$. Since $k\ge c(i+1)$, stabilization at $i+1$ gives $x\in B_{i+1}$, and $f_i(x)=\varphi_{k,i}(z)=y$. Thus $(B_i,f_i|_{B_{i+1}})$ is a tower of nonempty sets with surjective transitions, and its compatible sequences are exactly those of $(E_i)$: any compatible $(e_i)$ satisfies $e_i=\varphi_{k,i}(e_k)\in B_i$ for $k\ge\max(i,c(i))$, while a compatible sequence in the $B_i$ is already one in the $E_i$.

source.place: Algebra, Example 0596 (example-ML-surjective-maps), algebra.tex lines 20736--20745: stable-image tower with surjective maps and unchanged limit; surjectivity calculation expanded

proof.text: Choose $b_1\in B_1$. Given $b_i\in B_i$, surjectivity in Step 2 gives $b_{i+1}\in B_{i+1}$ with $f_i(b_{i+1})=b_i$. Dependent choice makes these successive choices into one sequence $(b_i)_{i\ge1}$; it is compatible at every level, hence belongs to $\varprojlim_iB_i$. By Step 2 the same sequence belongs to $\varprojlim_iE_i$, proving the latter nonempty.
